papers.title_en: Retrospective macromolecular pool fraction mapping from conventional clinical MRI: a physics-guided self-supervised deep learning framework
papers.authors: Jelmer van Lune, Miha Fuderer, Oscar van der Heide, Matteo Maspero, Martin B. Schilder, Jan Willem Dankbaar, Stefano Mandija, Alessandro Sbrizzi
papers.evidence: 物理引导自监督深度学习用于脑MRI生物标志物映射
papers.tldr: 大分子池分数（MPF）对髓鞘完整性敏感，但依赖专门的定量磁化转移（qMT）采集，难以大规模应用。作者提出物理引导的自监督深度学习框架，嵌入双池磁化转移解析模型，并用自适应实例归一化适配不同采集参数，从常规T1、T2、FLAIR图像回顾性估计MPF。在7705次多中心3T扫描上训练评估，测试集白质MPF约0.182、灰质约0.144，病灶较正常白质低35.6%，跨协议一致性良好。该工作为利用既有临床影像档案研究脱髓鞘病理提供了可扩展途径。
papers.abstract_en: Macromolecular pool fraction (MPF) is a quantitative imaging biomarker sensitive to myelin integrity and other changes in tissue macromolecular content, but specialized acquisitions and reconstruction methods limit its use in large-scale studies. We present a physics-guided, self-supervised deep learning framework for retrospectively estimating MPF directly from conventional clinical brain MRI ($T_1$-weighted, $T_2$-weighted, and fluid-attenuated inversion recovery [FLAIR]) without paired quantitative reference scans. The framework embeds an analytical two-pool magnetization transfer signal model that related sequence-averaged radiofrequency transmit power to apparent longitudinal relaxation. To accommodate heterogeneous clinical protocols, the network conditions intermediate features on acquisition parameters via adaptive instance normalization. It was trained and evaluated on a multisite, multivendor, multiprotocol dataset of 7,705 MRI sessions (3 T). Across 1,237 test sessions, mean MPF was $0.182 \pm 0.007$ in white matter and $0.144 \pm 0.009$ in gray matter, with limited variation across vendor-by-protocol groups (between-group coefficient of variation: 2.65% and 5.63%, respectively). In 70 sessions with demyelinating-disease labels, MPF was 35.6% lower in segmented lesions than in normal-appearing white matter. MPF maps from two different clinical protocols acquired in a healthy volunteer showed a mean voxel-wise absolute percentage difference of 7.7% and a concordance correlation coefficient of $0.888$, indicating good cross-protocol consistency. These results suggest that magnetization transfer-informed self-supervised learning enables stable MPF mapping from conventional clinical MRI, providing a scalable approach to investigate demyelinating pathology in both existing imaging archives and prospectively acquired conventional clinical scans without dedicated qMT acquisitions.

papers.title_en: MtReNIRS: A Self-Supervised Foundation Model for Transferable Neurovascular Representations
papers.authors: Tony Chae, Kleanthis Avramidis, Dimitra Emmanouilidou, Ivan J. Tashev
papers.evidence: 面向 fNIRS 神经血管表示的自监督基础模型，属于神经影像 AI 医疗
papers.tldr: fNIRS建模受限于小规模单会话、低采样及设备布局异质，难获跨被试、任务和设备的通用表征。MtReNIRS以布局感知掩码自编码器，在12个公开数据集（268人、567小时）上预训练，将异质布局映射到共享解剖参考，并联合编码慢血流、色团与皮层位置。模型在三个外部数据集上迁移，跨被试性能不逊全监督基线，少样本校准优于先前最优且对稀疏布局稳健。这表明布局感知自监督可学习生理基础扎实、可迁移的fNIRS表征，支撑标签高效脑机接口。
papers.abstract_en: Functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) offers a promising approach for monitoring the hemodynamic correlates of neural activity in naturalistic settings. However, existing modeling methods for fNIRS are largely confined to small-scale, single-session data with low sampling rates, driven by high heterogeneity in acquisition devices and optode montages. In addition, the complex spatiotemporal structure of fNIRS signals further restricts model scalability and transferability across settings. As a result, it remains unclear whether a single fNIRS encoder can learn representations that are usable across subjects, tasks, devices, and montages. Here, we show that a montage-aware masked autoencoder, pretrained on 12 public fNIRS datasets spanning 268 subjects and 567 recording hours, learns generalizable neurovascular representations that transfer across three external datasets. Our fNIRS foundation model, MtReNIRS, jointly encodes the slow hemodynamic nature of fNIRS, chromophore identity and cortical location by mapping heterogeneous montages onto a shared anatomical reference. MtReNIRS achieves cross-subject performance on par or better than fully supervised baselines and excels in few-shot within-subject calibration, where it outperforms prior state-of-the-art fNIRS models, while remaining robust to sparse montages. Our results indicate that montage-aware self-supervision yields physiologically grounded, transferable fNIRS representations, providing a scalable foundation for label-efficient brain-computer interfaces.

papers.title_en: Towards fNIRS foundation models: A curated corpus of 67 public datasets with channel positions in MNI space
papers.evidence: 神经影像AI医疗：面向脑基础模型的67个公开fNIRS数据集精选语料库，并统一到MNI空间
papers.tldr: fNIRS基础模型受限于公开数据规模小、协议设备与导联配置异质，且缺乏跨数据集可比通道位置。作者整理67个公开数据集，覆盖2798名受试者、1955小时，提取HbO/HbR信号并将各通道定位到MNI标准空间。同时发布自动数据加载器与最小预处理流程，这是迄今最大规模fNIRS数据整理工作。该资源旨在降低任务特定数据依赖，为fNIRS基础模型的大规模预训练与跨数据集建模提供统一语料和工具。
papers.abstract_en: Brain foundation models have transformed medical artificial intelligence and computational neuroscience by reducing the reliance on task-specific data through large-scale pretraining. While they have been successful with non-invasive neuroimaging data, their adoption in functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) has lagged due to the limited size and heterogeneity of public datasets, which are collected under varying protocols, devices, and sensor configurations. In addition, no single fNIRS dataset is comparable in size to the largest datasets in functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI), electroencephalography (EEG), or magnetoencephalography (MEG). The fNIRS datasets are also spread across different platforms and often have insufficient information, or lack the protocols that would make them easier to use. Given the advances in EEG foundation models that enable flexible modeling across diverse EEG montages, we curated 1,955 hours of fNIRS data from 67 public datasets spanning 2,798 participants, representing the largest fNIRS curation effort to date. The curated data include oxygenated (HbO) and deoxygenated (HbR) hemoglobin signals along with the three-dimensional position of every channel in the standard space of the Montreal Neurological Institute (MNI), which makes positions comparable across datasets. We release dataloaders that handle each dataset automatically, along with the minimal preprocessing pipeline used to prepare the data, at https://github.com/sposso/fnirs-datasets. This work aims to facilitate the future development of foundation models for fNIRS.
